finding_7_calendar_detector_has_emitted_.symptom_CONFIRMED: Across 99 historical calendar_status observations in docs/signals telemetry: unknown=65, open=18, off_market=9, closed=7. Date-bucketed, the picture is not a mix — it is a cutover. open/closed appear ONLY on 2026-07-15. off_market appears ONLY 2026-06-05..06-07. Every observation on 07-16, 07-17, 07-18 and 07-21 is 'unknown'. ~5 days, zero real values.
finding_7_calendar_detector_has_emitted_.why_this_is_invisible: 'unknown' is the CONSERVATIVE no-op value at every consumer. Step 4.3 suppresses only on [holiday,weekend] → never fires. Step 4.5 freshness downgrade requires calendar_status in [holiday,weekend] → never fires. bctc-offmarket on unknown → _cron_fallback:true → cron governs. So a dead detector produces no error, no log, no suppression — it silently disables every calendar-dependent gate while the tick still reports PRESSURE_MODE=adaptive. Same family as composite-score-masks-dead-detector and passive-health-masks-dead-data.
finding_7_calendar_detector_has_emitted_.observable_consequence: The 07-18/07-19 weekend ran with calendar_status=unknown, so weekend suppression of non-guaranteed slots did not fire. Whatever the adaptive layer was meant to save on weekends, it did not save.
finding_7_calendar_detector_has_emitted_.MECHANISM_UNDETERMINED: I have NOT established WHY. Candidates not yet discriminated: (a) the calendar detector/source broke or was removed ~07-16; (b) emit_pressure_state does not populate calendar_status and simply defaults it, so whichever caller last wrote the file determines the value; (c) an upstream calendar data source went stale. I am reporting a confirmed symptom, not a diagnosed cause. Do not let this file be read as a root-cause.
finding_7_calendar_detector_has_emitted_.caveat_on_my_own_evidence: 4 of the 07-21 'unknown' observations are my own emits this session. But 07-16/17/18 (28/17/15 observations) predate this session entirely, so the pattern is not an artifact of my ticks.
finding_7_calendar_detector_has_emitted_.owner: po → route to whoever owns pressure-state emission / cadence foundation (DWF-PHASE1).

finding_8_producer_consumer_value_domain.severity: MED — mostly latent TODAY, but it is a live landmine
finding_8_producer_consumer_value_domain.verified_in_code: scripts/agents-flow/cadence-policy.js:70-71 — unmatched lookup returns { interval_minutes: 240, _cron_fallback: false }, commented 'safe default (AC-P1-1-3)'.
finding_8_producer_consumer_value_domain.verified_in_data: docs/data/cadence-policy.json rows match exactly 5 calendar_status values: half_day, holiday, open, unknown, weekend.
finding_8_producer_consumer_value_domain.mismatch: The emitter has historically produced 'off_market' (9 obs) and 'closed' (7 obs). NEITHER is in the policy's 5-value domain. Any tick with those values matches no rule and silently takes the 240-minute generic default with _cron_fallback:false — i.e. the slot's declared policy is bypassed entirely and replaced by an undocumented second policy.
finding_8_producer_consumer_value_domain.why_it_is_only_latent_now: Those two values have not been emitted since 2026-07-15 (see finding_7). If the calendar detector is REPAIRED without also widening the policy domain, every repaired tick immediately starts hitting the 240-min default. The fix for finding_7 therefore ARMS finding_8. They must ship together.
finding_8_producer_consumer_value_domain.the_deeper_smell: A 'safe default' that silently substitutes a different cadence is not a fallback, it is a second policy with no name and no owner. It should log or fail loud on an unrecognised calendar_status rather than absorb it.
finding_8_producer_consumer_value_domain.claim_NOT_made: I did NOT execute snapToCronBoundary, so I am not stating the precise fire/suppress outcome per slot under the 240-min default. That depends on cron-period snapping I have not run.
